about: The mutant runner shares the capped-child classifier with proclimit.

mutants.name: gcoom-mutants-text-only
mutants.rule: A capped mutant child's span-queue allocation fault has reason memory.

mutants.name: fk7a-format-ignored
mutants.rule: A mutated source the formatter would rewrite is invalid, never killed: the runner's format check fails it whatever its edit means.

mutants.name: fk12a-refusal-ignored
mutants.rule: A mutated source the compiler refuses with a new diagnostic is invalid, never killed.

mutants.name: fk12a-declared-ignored
mutants.rule: A row that declares the refusal its point (refused) is judged by its tests: the refusal may kill it.

mutants.name: scope-select-ignored
mutants.rule: The coverage pass measures what the selected mutants need, not what -run leaves out.

mutants.name: scope-tools-ignored
mutants.rule: A suite whose tool (the ergo CLI, the examples runner) compiles a mutated package is measured.

mutants.name: scope-anchor-dropped
mutants.rule: A suite whose test a row names (killer or anchor) is measured, whether or not it compiles the mutated package (GT-BOUND merge: the coverage store keeps whole suites).

mutants.name: scope-deps-unread
mutants.rule: The scope reads what each test binary and tool compiles: a suite misread as compiling nothing would leave its mutants uncovered.

mutants.name: mutclean-copy-without-git
mutants.rule: The runner's copy carries the checkout's Git file list, so a test that reads the repository (git ls-files) can kill a mutant.

mutants.name: mutclean-other-package-killer-dropped
mutants.from: return Suite{Name: name, Package: "./" + dir, Tags: tags}, nil, true
mutants.rule: A killer in another package of the module (DIR or DIR[TAGS]) is a suite the runner runs, so no row is run by hand.

mutants.name: mutclean-ergo-suite-killer-dropped
mutants.rule: A package ledger's killer named by an ergo suite (lower, std, examples) runs in that suite, with its tools.

mutants.name: mutclean-work-shared
mutants.rule: The default -work is a directory of one run: two runs at once never share coverage counters.

mutants.name: mutclean-work-kept
mutants.rule: The default -work is removed at the end of its run.

mutants.name: xpkg-named-killer-not-run
mutants.rule: A ledger's named killer runs whether or not the coverage pass saw it reach the mutated lines: a test in another package kills through a program it builds.

mutants.name: xpkg-select-ignored
mutants.rule: Only the selected rows bring killer suites: a run of one row builds the suites that row names, not every killer suite of its ledger.

mutants.name: xpkg-note-kept
mutants.rule: A note after a killer's test name (past a space) is the reader's: the runner runs the test it names.

mutants.name: xpkg-named-dropped
mutants.rule: Every suite records the tests the ledgers name, so a Go suite missing one is refused and a command suite runs a named example that is not a default.

mutants.name: xpkg-example-ledger-own-suite
mutants.rule: A ledger whose directory has no Go tests (an example's, editing .ergo files) brings no suite of its own, which would not build; its named killers judge it.

mutants.name: xpkg-stale-killer-accepted
mutants.rule: A Go suite that lacks a test a ledger names is refused before the mutant pass.
mutants.gap: No runner test builds a suite missing a named test; internal/residue:TestLedgerEditsApplyOnce refuses such a row in the checkout's ledgers before any run (ledger-killer-alias).

				if !slices.Contains(names, n) {
mutants.rule: A command suite (the examples) runs a named example that is not a default one.
mutants.gap: The fake module of TestRunnerMatchesModel has Go suites only; the affected run of scripts/examples' ledger (examples:router) exercises it.

mutants.name: b18-nested-killer-from-root
mutants.to: if mod := nestedModule(root, dir); false && mod != "" {
mutants.rule: A killer in a nested Go module (selfhost's hostsyntax) is built in that module; from the checkout's root go test refuses it and the run fails.

mutants.name: b18-nested-package-covered
mutants.rule: A package of a nested module is no -coverpkg package of the checkout: naming it fails every suite's coverage build.

mutants.name: b18-nested-coverdir
mutants.rule: A nested module's suite is built without coverage, so its test binary takes no -test.gocoverdir; with it the killer fails on the unmutated tree and kills nothing.
mutants.gap: No runner test builds a nested module's suite; the affected run of internal/selfhostcheck's ledger (r4-m2.log: hostsyntax:TestFamiliesCoverSyntax failed on the unmutated tree) exercises it.

mutants.name: mutnames-unresolved-suite-skipped
mutants.from: unresolved = append(unresolved, fmt.Errorf("%s: mutant %q: %q names no suite
mutants.to: _ = append(unresolved, fmt.Errorf("%s: mutant %q: %q names no suite
mutants.rule: A killer or anchor id whose suite resolves to nothing is an error of the ledger, never a killer the runner leaves out.

mutants.name: mutnames-missing-test-accepted
mutants.rule: A killer or anchor id names a test its suite has (a Test func of the package, an example program); a renamed or deleted test is an error of the ledger.

mutants.name: mutnames-ledger-env-dropped
mutants.rule: A package ledger's env is the environment of every run of its own suite, so a plain runner invocation judges killers that need a switch (tsproj's ERGO_TS_TEST=1).

mutants.name: mutnames-ergo-ledger-env-accepted
mutants.rule: check's and lower's ledgers share the ergo suites; an env there is refused, not dropped or spread to every suite.

mutants.name: mutnames-plain-rerun-dropped
mutants.rule: A test that fails only when its binary is built with coverage (a sandboxed self-run) and passes without stays a killer; it is not dropped as failing on the unmutated tree.

mutants.name: mutnames-no-test-timeout
mutants.rule: A Go test binary runs with a -test.timeout, as under go test, so a test that bounds its children by t.Deadline judges mutants.

mutants.name: gt2-edit-unkeyed
mutants.rule: A row's key holds its edit: an edited row is judged again.

mutants.name: gt2-closure-unkeyed
mutants.rule: A row's key holds every file its Go killers read.

mutants.name: gt2-whole-dropped
mutants.rule: A killer that is no Go package of the module keys the row on every source.

mutants.name: gt2-ignored-unkeyed
mutants.rule: A row's key holds the ignored files its Go killers read.

mutants.name: gt2-relative-root
mutants.rule: A relative -root still finds its packages' closures; else every row is keyed on every file.

mutants.name: gt2-no-reuse
mutants.from: if r, ok := lookup(key); ok && storable(m, r) {
mutants.to: if r, ok := lookup(key); false && ok && storable(m, r) {
mutants.rule: A row whose key is unchanged reuses its stored killed verdict.

mutants.name: gt2-ledger-order
mutants.rule: Reused and judged verdicts are reported in ledger order.

mutants.name: gt6-key-closure-dropped
mutants.from:
if closure == nil || closure.Covers(p) {
			put("file", p, in.files[p])
mutants.to:
if closure == nil {
			put("file", p, in.files[p])
mutants.rule: A suite's segment key holds the content of every file in its closure.

mutants.name: gt6-key-ignored-dropped
mutants.rule: A Go suite's segment key holds the ignored files its closure reads (generated testdata).

mutants.name: gt6-store-failed
mutants.rule: A segment with a test that failed on the unmutated tree is not stored.

mutants.name: gt6-ends-unchecked
mutants.rule: A segment whose suite's key changed during the measure is not stored.

mutants.name: gt6-merge-offset
mutants.rule: Merged segments keep each block's tests: indexes move by the tests before the segment.

mutants.name: gt6-segment-tools
mutants.rule: A suite's segment keeps the build times of the tools it runs (the mutant pass's build deadlines).

mutants.name: gt6-no-reuse
mutants.to: if c, ok := load(keys[s.Name]); false && ok {
mutants.rule: A suite whose key is unchanged takes its stored segment and is not measured.

mutants.name: gt6-tree-no-store
mutants.rule: The runner's coverage pass takes the stored segments when a store is named.

mutants.name: gt7-no-increment
mutants.from:
case cur != nil:
			next := ergoPos{cur.file, cur.line + 1}
mutants.to:
case cur != nil:
			next := ergoPos{cur.file, cur.line}
mutants.rule: Each Go line after a //line directive is one .ergo line on.

mutants.name: gt7-func-keeps-position
mutants.rule: A top-level func starts with no position: a std body, written without directives, maps to no .ergo line of the program.

mutants.name: gt7-inline-not-carried
mutants.rule: The lines after an inline /*line*/ directive go on from its position.

mutants.name: gt7-tag-kept
mutants.rule: An inlined body's directive (FILE#ergo-inline-N) names FILE.

mutants.name: gt7-any-base
mutants.rule: A block the cover tool names by a directive's base name maps only to lines of files with that name.

mutants.name: gt7-outside-root
mutants.from: if err != nil || rel == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(rel, "../") || filepath.IsAbs(rel) {
mutants.rule: A directive to a file outside the checkout copy maps to no checkout file.

mutants.name: gt7-column-as-line
mutants.rule: A directive FILE:LINE:COL names LINE, not COL.

mutants.name: gt7-env-dropped
mutants.rule: The coverage pass's children build the programs they lower as coverage builds, so .ergo lines are covered.
mutants.gap: Only an end-to-end coverage pass that builds the ergo CLI with coverage and runs a lowered example sees it (GT7 acceptance, gate2/GT7/accept.ts); no test of the package builds the CLI.

mutants.name: gt7b-mark-ignored
mutants.from: if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(strings.TrimLeft(line, "\t "), coverMark); ok {
mutants.to: if rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(strings.TrimLeft(line, "\t "), coverMark); false && ok {
mutants.rule: A cover mark gives the next Go line its std .ergo position.

mutants.name: gt7b-mark-moves-go
mutants.rule: A cover mark is a comment: it moves no Go position, so the cover tool's name of a block after it is still the Go file's or the last directive's.

mutants.name: gt7b-std-tree
mutants.rule: A cover mark's std/… path is the checkout's internal/sketch/std/….

mutants.name: gt7b-sub-dir
mutants.rule: A block of a package below the copy's root (KEY/p/NAME) is read from that package's Go files.

mutants.name: gt7b-e2e-mode-set
mutants.rule: The tests of the coverage pass count in the mode the programs they build count in: go tool covdata refuses two modes in one directory.
mutants.gap: Only an end-to-end coverage pass sees it (GT7b acceptance, gate2/GT7b/accept.ts: rpc-mount-exact covered by the rpcgen loopback, cu6-into-hops-lost by lower:TestHTTPNetworkRuns); no test of the package runs the coverage pass.

mutants.name: gt8-no-testlog
mutants.rule: Each Go test of the coverage pass writes the go command's test log, so the files it opens are known.

mutants.name: gt8-reads-ignored
mutants.rule: A test that opens a file of the checkout covers that file's mutants.

mutants.name: gt8-relative-root
mutants.rule: A relative name in the test log is relative to the test's working directory (its package directory), not the checkout root.

mutants.name: gt8-readers-skipped
mutants.rule: The readers of a file cover every line of it.

mutants.name: gt8b-var-unset
mutants.rule: The coverage pass's tests note their embedded reads.
mutants.gap: Only a real coverage pass sees it (GT8b acceptance, gate2/GT8b/accept.ts: check's seal-callback-params on std/http/http.ergo, unnamed, is killed by check:TestSealingIsTheVisibilityRule); TestRunnerMatchesModel's fake module embeds nothing and always covers a package.

mutants.name: gt8b-gocoverdir-uncovered
mutants.rule: A suite built without coverage (a ledger of .ergo rows only) runs without -test.gocoverdir, which would fail every test on the unmutated tree.
mutants.gap: Only a real coverage pass sees it (GT8b acceptance, gate2/GT8b/accept.ts: check's seal-callback-params on std/http/http.ergo, unnamed, is killed by check:TestSealingIsTheVisibilityRule); TestRunnerMatchesModel's fake module embeds nothing and always covers a package.

mutants.name: gt8b-goflags-p
mutants.rule: A child of the runner sees no GOFLAGS: a set GOFLAGS makes ergo build refuse its direct path, so cmd/ergo's direct-path tests fail on the unmutated tree.

mutants.name: gt8b-red-judged
mutants.rule: A row that a test failing on the unmutated tree covers or names gets no verdict.

mutants.name: gt8b-unjudged-exit
mutants.rule: An unjudged row fails the run.

mutants.name: gtc-compile-counted
mutants.rule: A mutant whose file does not compile is invalid, never killed by a test that fails on the compile error.

mutants.name: gtc-invalid-exit
mutants.rule: An invalid row fails the run.

mutants.name: gtc-std-unchecked
mutants.rule: A std .ergo row is compiled by checking the copy's std.
mutants.gap: Only a real pass over a std or Ergo-module row sees it (GT-COMPILE sweep, gate2/GT-COMPILE/sweep.sh: -compiles over every ledger); TestRunnerMatchesModel's fake module has no .ergo file.

mutants.name: gtc-ergo-unchecked
mutants.rule: A row of an Ergo module's .ergo file is compiled by the copy's ergo check of its directory.
mutants.gap: Only a real pass over a std or Ergo-module row sees it (GT-COMPILE sweep, gate2/GT-COMPILE/sweep.sh: -compiles over every ledger); TestRunnerMatchesModel's fake module has no .ergo file.

mutants.name: gtc-baseline-ignored
mutants.rule: A file that fails to compile unmutated (a fixture) makes no row of it invalid.
mutants.gap: No fixture of the fake module fails to compile unmutated; the sweep over every ledger would list such rows invalid.

mutants.name: gtb-embedder-none
mutants.rule: A mutant of a file that is not Go counts as the package that embeds it: the suites that compile that package are measured.
